proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the sharp fixed-ratio RMST risk law, product-limit attainment, Gaussian and Greenwood inference, and the incident-only separation; the D0.5 math referee passed and both cited sources were attested. The field-tier package did not land because the broader source-ratio frontier and application evidence remained open, and the general referee capped the delivered score at 7.1 below the 7.4 field threshold. A future re-raise needs a new anchor that resolves the frontier and the 2024 combined-cohort priority question.
tldr: For a new freely stratified triangular \(C^2\) submodel of stationary combined incident and prevalent sampling, an incident cohort of order \(n/\log n\) repairs the treatment-origin information deficit of an order-\(n\) prevalent cohort. The pooled delayed-entry product-limit estimator of the known-weight causal RMST contrast has sharp local minimax risk \(C(P)\log\log n/n\), a uniform Gaussian limit, consistent Greenwood studentization, and uniformly honest Wald coverage. A capped reciprocal-score converse preserves the full constant at this design and reveals a separate smoothness elbow near \(N^{-1/6}\); the maximal source-ratio frontier remains open. The larotrectinib external-control analysis motivates treatment-initiation RMST and delayed entry, but its observed controls are not asserted to be a stationary prevalent sample.
gap: Fixed-positive source-fraction asymptotics do not permit substituting an incident fraction that tends to zero. Existing causal analysis of combined incident and prevalent observational cohorts uses propensity-score methodology and a Cox model under a fixed regular regime, while fixed-mix risk-set formulas identify the early-time denominator. Neither line establishes a sharp triangular minimax constant for standardized RMST, actual pooled-product-limit mean-square attainment, or feasible uniform Greenwood studentization.
fill: Derive the cellwise information coefficient, prove a stopped uniform \(L^2\) expansion for the reported product-limit RMST, match it with smooth triangular lower-bound paths, and retain the random compensator together with an explicit exponentially small zero-variance-event bound in Greenwood inference.
